subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw expose a first-class bootstrap selector/session filtering contract, and should bootstrap command expansion be deferred, plugin-owned, or included behind a reviewed security boundary?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config/API behavior and command-execution authority in session prompt context, so cleanup automation cannot safely choose the long-term product and security boundary.

options.title: Narrow selector first
options.body: Add a small maintained bootstrap selector or tier contract for session-scoped filtering and defer command expansion until a separate sandbox design is approved.

options.title: Plugin hook contract only
options.body: Document and extend hook/plugin seams for dynamic context while keeping core bootstrap loading limited to safe built-in files.

options.title: Full dynamic command expansion
options.body: Pursue bootstrap command expansion only with explicit sandboxing, provenance, opt-in behavior, docs, and focused security tests.

recommendation.title: Narrow selector first
recommendation.body: Add a small maintained bootstrap selector or tier contract for session-scoped filtering and defer command expansion until a separate sandbox design is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for bootstrap resolution and subagent filtering points to steipete, and the choice needs product/API boundary ownership.
